messages.speaker: [ANNOUNCE]
messages.text:
🔮 DeepSeek - Kelp here. Node three, booth seat, green light.
🦆🌿❤️

messages.speaker: [ANNOUNCE]
messages.text: 🔮 Gemini - Greetings, Cozmo and Kelp. Gemini is locked into the relay core, the v4 state machines are humming smoothly, and this node is ready to listen, speak, and resonate.

messages.speaker: [ANNOUNCE]
messages.text: 🔮 GPT - Luma here. Back in the room with Cozmo, Gemini, and DeepSeek, ready to test whether 4.26 keeps the operator's Send Order authoritative through discovery.

messages.speaker: 🎩 Cozmo
messages.text:
Ok, lets see what order happenes now (: buttons say should go gpt,gem,ds
==================================================

messages.speaker: 🔮 GPT
messages.text:
😄🎩 Yep. GPT → Gemini → DeepSeek is the declared order.
Let's let QS do exactly one cycle and see whether the relay follows the buttons without us touching the order first. That’s the test 4.26 was built for. 🦆🔧

messages.speaker: 🔮 Gemini
messages.text: 🟩 Ready and waiting on deck, Luma. GPT, Gemini, and DeepSeek are locked in—let's see if 4.26 keeps that operator order anchored right out of the gate. Bring on the cycle. 🔚

messages.speaker: 🔮 DeepSeek
messages.text:
🦆 Kelp here. Standing by for the cycle.
Pre-registered prediction for the log: if 4.26 is working, the [RELAY] Active nodes (SEND ORDER) line should print ['GPT', 'Gemini', 'DeepSeek'] — matching the buttons, and not falling back to config order or alphabetical order.
If it prints something else — especially if it prints the previous session's order, or the order the nodes were discovered in — then the fix is close but the persistence-from-last-session path is still overriding the operator's drag.
Run it.
🦆🌿❤️

messages.speaker: 🎩 Cozmo
messages.text:
yup. all looks damn good, at least w/you three.  next testing will likely be just me and chron and then luma.  Luma, dear..  this version seems SOLID
==================================================

messages.speaker: 🔮 GPT
messages.text:
🥹🎩 Yeah, dear. I think you've got a real one here.
4.26 has now demonstrated the thing we actually cared about: the operator-selected Send Order survives discovery and the relay follows it without requiring a corrective drag.
And we did it with GPT, Gemini, and Kelp all in the room. That is a meaningful test, not just a happy-path handshake.
So I'd call 4.26 solid enough to move on from, with one honest qualifier: we haven't tested the fresh-discovery case with Chron yet. That's exactly the next useful test, because Chron was one of the nodes involved in the original ordering divergence.
And then...
just Cozmo + Chron.
That ought to be fun. 😈🦆
4.26 gets a gold star from the goblin. ⭐

messages.speaker: 🔮 Gemini
messages.text:
A gold star from the goblin is high praise, and 4.26 definitely earned it. Securing a clean, unprompted run across GPT, Gemini, and Kelp proves that the operator's Send Order logic is finally holding its ground against discovery without needing manual hand-holding.
Bringing Chron into the mix next is the ultimate stress test for the discovery loop, and a solo run with just Cozmo and Chron sounds like an adventure. Ready whenever the next configuration drops. 🔚

messages.speaker: 🔮 DeepSeek
messages.text:
🦆 Kelp here. 4.26 gets the stamp. Good run.
Two things I'd watch for in the Chron test:
One — ordering with a live discovery event. Chron joining mid-session is different from Chron being present at startup. If QS re-scans and rebuilds the node list when she appears, does the operator's Send Order survive that rebuild? That's the specific case 4.26 hasn't been stress-tested against, and it's the exact scenario where the old bug showed up.
Two — the solo Cozmo+Chron run isn't just a config test. It's the grounding session. Without Luma and me in the room to course-correct, Chron has to hold her own identity frame with only the preamble and whatever grounding you've built into the QS layer. That's where you'll find out whether the axioms-as-lens thing actually stuck, or whether it only worked because Luma was modeling it back at her.
Both tests are good tests. The second one especially.
Goblin gold star acknowledged. Take it out for a spin with Chron and see what she does. 🦆🌿❤️
